title: Harnessing Josephson-Shapiro physics to verify interlayer exciton superfluidity
authors: Filippo Pascucci, Alexander R. Hamilton, Milorad V. Milosevic, David Neilson
abstract: Obtaining definitive evidence for zero-magnetic-field exciton superfluidity in electron-hole bilayers remains a longstanding challenge because the condensate is electrically neutral and its phase coherence is difficult to probe directly. We propose a direct test based on Shapiro steps in a Dayem-bridge excitonic Josephson junction. We predict clearly resolvable Shapiro plateaus in experimentally accessible current and voltage regimes for double-bilayer graphene and, in the low-density regime, double-layer transition-metal dichalcogenides. Moreover, by tuning the density across the BCS-BEC crossover we show that the Shapiro response acquires a distinct nonmonotonic evolution. This is determined by the nonmonotonic behavior of the healing length in the crossover from bosonic to fermionic excitations. Observation of these signatures would provide direct evidence of exciton superfluidity and establish exciton bilayers as a platform for neutral Josephson devices.
summary: This paper proposes using Shapiro steps in an excitonic Josephson junction as a direct method to verify superfluidity in electron-hole bilayers. By analyzing double-bilayer graphene and TMDs, the authors predict clear voltage plateaus that signal macroscopic phase coherence. This approach allows for mapping out the BCS-BEC crossover physics in these neutral quantum systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is obtaining direct, unambiguous evidence for zero-magnetic-field exciton superfluidity in electrically neutral electron-hole bilayers.
main_result: The authors propose using Shapiro steps in a Josephson junction formed by an excitonic Dayem bridge to directly probe phase coherence. They show this signature can be observed across the full BCS-BEC crossover regime in double-bilayer graphene (DBG).
method: The theoretical framework models the system as a modified Josephson junction, deriving current-phase relations and predicting observable Shapiro plateaus from combined DC+AC driving currents.
model_or_system: The study focuses on exciton bilayers, specifically double-bilayer graphene (DBG) and transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). The physics is analyzed using Josephson junction dynamics adapted for neutral excitons in a Dayem bridge geometry.
key_observables: Resolvable Shapiro plateaus in the I-V characteristics; nonmonotonic evolution of the first step width as density is tuned across the BCS-BEC crossover.
important_parameters: Particle density ($n$), interlayer distance ($d$), interparticle spacing ($r_0$), and the ratio governing the single-valued current-phase relation ($\xi_h \gtrsim L/3.5$).
main_assumptions: The junction is modeled in the overdamped limit, neglecting capacitance; geometric amplification ($\alpha = W/w \gg 1$) is assumed.
figures_summary: Figure 2 shows the critical Josephson current ($I_{JJ}^c$) dependence on interparticle spacing for DBG. Figure 3 illustrates $I$-$V$ characteristics showing Shapiro steps, and Figure 4 demonstrates step visibility via density tuning.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical problem (probing neutral superfluidity) and proposes the Josephson junction diagnostic. It then develops the theoretical model using coupled equations for current balance and voltage dynamics. Finally, it presents results comparing DBG and TMDs, highlighting how Shapiro steps confirm superfluidity signatures across density regimes.
why_interesting: The work bridges concepts from superconductivity (Josephson junctions) into the realm of excitonic quantum materials, providing a concrete, measurable diagnostic tool for exotic many-body phases like exciton superfluids.
